[Editor's note: This was the era when mono mixes for UK pop records were the norm and most of the effort was put into creating them. Singles were king in the UK and they were in mono, which was in keeping with the majority of domestic equipment, few people owning the more expensive stereo turntables. Indeed until the late 60s/early 70s stereo mixes were often an after thought in the studio as well as being rushed, often being left to recording engineers, rather than the producer, to complete – which was even the case with The Beatles and Sgt Pepper. The pop radio stations of the mid to late 60s (Radio Luxembourg, the pirates and then BBC Radio 1) were all mono and it wasn't until 1973 that Radio 1 started regularly broadcasting in stereo.]
